qt: to the Commission Kosma Złotowski (ECR) Subject:

The Commission designated EUROCONTROL as the Network Manager for air traffic management for the period of 2020 to 20291. EUROCONTROL awarded the contract to Indra to modernise the integrated Network Management (iNM) flow management system, worth approximately EUR 370 million. According to information that emerged in 2026, the contract was reportedly terminated early owing to contractual breaches, particularly concerning the European Aeronautical Database, by means of a confidential settlement agreement providing for a payment of EUR 10.8 million to Indra. The agreement was reportedly concluded directly by EUROCONTROL’s Director General, without the approval of either the Member States or the Commission, and its terms have not been made public despite requests from the Member States, who fund the Network Manager. In this context: 1.
What supervisory powers did the Commission exercise over the Network Manager, and does it intend to request that EUROCONTROL fully disclose the agreement with Indra?
What measures does it intend to take to ensure that the Network Manager acts in the public interest and is subject to adequate governance controls, including when it comes to the next designation?

Has the iNM programme received EU funding? If so, does the Commission consider that there are grounds for European Anti-Fraud Office to intervene, given that EUROCONTROL, an international organisation, is not subject to national anticorruption legislation?

Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2019/709 of 6 May 2019 on the appointment of the network manager for air traffic management (ATM) network functions of the single European sky (ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dec_impl/2019/709/oj). 1
